faces.f: "We prepare for the known with daggers, rations, rope, and pitons. But we also prepare for the unknown with billycat tails, pikku roots, hedron chips . . ."

"Trust me, your lost fingers and toes are nothing compared to the lost treasures of Sejiri."
—Zahr Gada, Halimar expedition leader

"Not too bright, but good enough for the job required—carrying and walking in a straight line."
—Bruse Tarl, Goma Fada nomad
Upon such armor, even a mountain would break.
"The crossing demands singular focus. Your life consists of these ropes, these hooks, and these rocky crags. Your past is miles below."

"I have seen planes leveled and all life rendered to dust. It brought no pleasure, even to a heart as dark as mine."
—Sorin Markov

"Goddess, grant us light to banish the world's shadows."
—Prayer to Kamsa
When the earth shudders, the sky overflows.

"If survival is a game, I've seen the winner."
—Hazir, Sejiri cartographer
No more shall the righteous cower before evil.
"If you hire a sell-sword, you'd better watch your back. Hire me, and I'll watch it for you."
Kor have no concept of exploration. They return to homelands forgotten.
"Swords cannot reach far enough. Chains cannot strike hard enough. An eternal dilemma, but a simple one."
"For us, a rope represents the ties that bind the kor. For you, it's more literal."
"We take only what we need to survive. Believe me, you will need this."
"Why keep such trinkets? They only add weight to your travels."
"Sometimes I snare the unexpected, but I know its purpose will be revealed in time."

"Honor this place, for our children's children will stand here and speak these same words again."
—Ayli, Kamsa cleric
The more who rely on him, the more resolute he becomes.

"A good explorer has to be as slippery as a gomazoa, as tough as a scute bug, and luckier than a ten-fingered trapfinder."
—Arhana, Kazandu trapfinder
Explorers may find ways into the Sky Ruin, but they find its secrets well protected by shifting hedrons and Roil winds.
Most spirits are chained to this world by their despair, but he remains tethered by his hope for better days.
A cleric's true balm is the confidence he inspires in his compatriots.
These stubborn and unpredictable oxen inspire the plains nomads' most colorful curses.
Each spike is poisoned—the trapmaker's idea of mercy.

"Should you fall in the wilds, lift your voice to the Sky Realm. The one who answers will be your salvation."
—Emeria's Creed

"Even land dwellers may call for Emeria's grace in times of need."
—Emeria's Creed
Nothing quickens the predator's blood like the unfamiliar scents of new hunting grounds and the mewling cries of new prey.
The merfolk call the sky goddess Emeria. The kor call her Kamsa. The two races agree on little except that she offers many blessings to the faithful.

"Why fight the world when you know who will win?"
—Nissa Revane
"Some merfolk choose to rest their fins in the water. I believe wisdom exists not only where we were born but where we were told not to go."
Zendikar's volatile mana is the basis for many spectacular spells—and some equally astonishing failures.
She watches the chaos created by the Roil, seeking strength in the patterns of anarchy.
To explorers, "point man" is a polite way of saying "gomazoa fodder."
Hedrons perplex minds both great and small.
"Roil tide! Roil tide! Tie yourselves down!"
A spike and a maul are needed to crack their shells, but the taste is worth the effort.
Suddenly, Zurdi didn't care about treasure, glory, food . . . or the drakes circling above.
At low tide it slumbers. At high tide it devours.
When Lorthos emerges from his deepwater realm, the tides bow to his will and the coastline cowers in his presence.
"Many voices are needed to quiet this land."

"Do they seek knowledge or wealth? Are they bandits or benefactors? It depends on who is chanting the tale."
—Nikou, Joraga bard

"Life is a maze. This is one of its dead ends."
—Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
The Halimar Sea Caves are both the breeding ground of giant squids and the dumping ground of hardened criminals.
"Any good prospector must sift the gold from the sand."
A vortex that devours everything—even the souls of the living.

"He's a living library. He remembers everything our band of explorers has seen, and we can use that to our advantage."
—Zahr Gada, Halimar expedition leader
"The sky is like another sea. It teems with currents, life, and endless possibility."

"It's like a reef that runs aground on ships."
—Jaby, Silundi Sea nomad

"Hold up your spears. And try not to look like food."
—Tarsa, Sea Gate sell-sword

"There's a hole in your plan."
—Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage

"Even if the sphinxes do know the location of every relic, getting one to talk is harder than just searching yourself."
—Sachir, Akoum Expeditionary House
Most inhabitants of Zendikar have given up on the idea of an accurate map.

"I don't need to have the perfect plan. My foe just has to have an imperfect one."
—Jace Beleren

"At some point, every trapfinder will lose a hunk of flesh. It's just a question of how much—and whether it'll grow back."
—Arhana, Kazandu trapfinder
"Trapmaking is an art. The trap is a corporeal riddle, a battle of wits between its creator and whatever it lures inside."
Messenger, weapon, friend.

"The sky hedrons are covered with tern nests. It's as though the birds have given up on the land altogether."
—Ilori, merfolk falconer

"The best spot to hook one is right behind the gills."
—Rana Cloudwake, kor skyfisher
A drop now is all he needs to find you later.
A wraith is a tale of brutal slaying told anew whenever it finds a victim.
The tender light of the living quickens the pulse of the dead.

"The land is swollen with mana, cursed relics, and secrets. If you puncture it, you never know what will burst out."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
"Brave scar or unfortunate tale? It all depends on your pain threshold."

"The vampires of this world don't know the pleasures of hunger. They gorge themselves without savoring the kill."
—Sorin Markov
"You may enter the city—once the toll is paid."
Its sting hurts, but death is strangely painless.
Few among the living understand just how much of their world is shaped by the ruins of the dead.
"A creature's bloodscent is a beacon that cannot be disguised."
The creatures of Zendikar are opportunists, eating whatever is available to them. Like goblins. Or boats.
"When exploring the darkest regions, wickedness can be the best accomplice of all."
Hanging on the walls of his lair, the fallen halos cast his depravity in everlasting light.

"A little dark magic won't stop me. The worse the curse, the better the prize."
—Radavi, Joraga relic hunter, last words

"Guard your thoughts. You never know who might wish to take them from you."
—Kalitas, Bloodchief of Ghet
Only a bloodchief can create vampires. The rest sire nulls, who become mindless beasts in their former bodies.

"Is there anything in Guul Draz that *doesn't* suck the life out of you?"
—Tarsa, Sea Gate sell-sword
The traps around the vampire city of Malakir hint at the thirst of its inhabitants.

"He asked if I had work for him. No wasn't the right answer."
—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House
His spark lost, he plots revenge upon the plane whose corrupting mana fractured his soul.
When the blood hunt lost its thrill, she looked for less tangible means of domination.
The lacerators cut themselves before each hunt. They must feed before the sun rises or bleed to death.
Those who dare stand in its path are either brave or mindless. Or in the case of goblins, both.

"This is why I hate settlements. They lull you into a false sense of security."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
Where life and force collide.

"Quit pontificating, mage. The last thing we want to do is give it more hot air."
—Tala Vertan, Makindi shieldmate
"I've been all over this world. I even remember some of those places."

"Goblins are cheap, but be careful. It's a lot easier to steal from a corpse than a customer."
—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House
War paint made from kolya fruit heightens senses and lessens fear. Unfortunately, fear is usually what keeps you alive.
There is no fondness between the hound and its master. There is only a common appreciation of the hunt.
He gets paid by the axe.
"Do you smell something burning?"
On expeditions, minotaurs are worth their weight in gold. Fortunately for their paymasters, most minotaurs don't know how much they weigh.

"Lighting a fire needs kindling and heat. You be the kindling. I'll bring the heat."
—Chandra Nalaar
The flame of anger is hard to douse once lit.

"Only the foolhardy would venture into the Akoum Mountains without a lullmage to tame the raging rocks and living fires."
—Sachir, Akoum Expeditionary House
"Fire is my accomplice. For enough coin, it can be yours as well."

"Kor armorers buy the scales and claws. Elf oracles buy the rest."
—Nablus, North Hada trapper
Not every intelligent being is interested in treasure and lost knowledge . . . or even the basics of speech.

"The land here seems to go out of its way to kill you."
—Chandra Nalaar

"Now I know why they call it Shatterskull Pass. Rocks fell all night like hammers smashing an anvil. It's no wonder the giants are angry all the time."
—Mitra, Bala Ged missionary

"Since when did 'AIIIEEEE!' become a negotiation tactic?"
—Nikou, Joraga bard
Goblin lessons include the 2,071 tips for survival. Frek only remembered 2,070.
Once thrown, twice burned.
Goblins are more aggressive with a crowd to cheer them on.
A long way down is shorter than you think.
"Danger! Danger! Come out of the safety of your holes!"
Its insatiable hunger quickly depletes a region of prey. It must migrate from place to place to feed its massive bulk.

"Surely we could tame something besides hurdas and pillarfield oxen!"
—Sheyda, Ondu gamekeeper
"The elders say Zendikar has no safe, peaceful places. How would they know? They've never looked."

"Don't be fooled. If it were as docile as it looks, it would've died off long ago."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
The other tribes call them fanatics, but none deny that the Mul Daya elves have an iron-strong bond to some force greater than themselves.
The Roil redraws the world as it passes, leaving only the hedrons unchanged.
Adventuring bards recite *Chanter's Epics*, never-ending tales that keep their comrades' minds alert to danger.
Its scales contain the essence of thousands of lotus blooms.
When civilization encroaches on nature, Zendikar encroaches back.
"Nissa will save the elves, but only the ones who have proved their worth."
"I'm strong enough to survive alone. I'm smart enough to want companions at my side."

"A might spell can be handy against baloths, giants, kraken, the Roil—or if you lose your bearings in the woods."
—Chadir the Navigator

"When the land is angry, so are they."
—Nissa Revane
There are many ruins, but there used to be many more.

"Sheath your swords! Cudgels only. I see a new pair of waterproof trek boots slithering away."
—Nablus, North Hada trapper
Some elves believe that their survival instincts are born of many cycles of reincarnation.

"Survival rule 781: There are always more scute bugs."
—Zurdi, goblin shortcutter
Instead of adapting to its environment, it adapts its environment to itself.

"The blood of the forest is beholden to no one."
—Nissa Revane
Sometimes violent earthquakes, hurtling boulders, and unseasonable dust storms are wrongly attributed to the Roil.
Its territory is defined by wherever it is at the moment.

"You can't trust your eyes. A tree might look healthy, but its insides tell a different tale."
—Zahr Gada, Halimar expedition leader
The lone wolf dies alone.

"I've known true ferocity and power. Those brazen 'planar-walkers' have no idea what wild really means."
—Chadir the Navigator
Expeditions follow the paths it leaves in its wake.
An explorer's essentials in a wild world.

"In these bloodstains I will find the fingerprints of our oppressors."
—Anowon, the Ruin Sage

"Gods don't die. They merely slumber."
—Ayli, Kamsa cleric

"I use maps to find out where explorers have already been. Then I go the other way."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
Part tool, part weapon, part of the kor.

"I don't care when the hedrons awoke. *Why* is the question that really matters."
—Anowon, the Ruin Sage
A fragment of ancient power lost in the heart of Ora Ondar.

"We suffer uneasy ground, unstable alliances, and unpredictable magic. Something you can truly trust is worth more than a chest of gold."
—Nikou, Joraga bard
It's much easier to list the places they *haven't* been.

"Until this expedition is done, that blade is your guardian, your liberator, and your best friend all rolled into one."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
Its crystalline core refracts light into chaos.
The fastest way across the dunes is above.

The Champion reached for a stone, and Heliod placed the sun into her hand.
—*The Theriad*

"No doubt the arbiters would put you away, after all the documents are signed. But I will have justice now."
—Alovnek, Boros guildmage
The Izzet mage knew she would neither get her thermoinverter back nor have the satisfaction of exploding it herself.
When the earth shudders, the sky overflows.
In the first moments, the gate to the afterlife opened, and the people were prostrate in the light of the God-Pharaoh.
Kor have no concept of exploration. They return to homelands forgotten.
A blazing sun that never sets.
"You can come back once you've learned some manners—and figured out how to reconstitute your physical forms."
Oona's song is like a twisted dinner chime. All the faeries return home, but it is Oona who feasts—on the stolen dreams and rumors they serve her.
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."
History may be written by the triumphant, but it's often rewritten by the troublesome.
"All that concerns me is the vampires' sense of smell and those freezing Nephalian nights."
The currents of the Marang wash away both tracks and blood.
Possession is ten-tenths of the law.
To know the battlefield is to anticipate the enemy. To know the enemy is to anticipate victory.

"We're on the fortieth floor, with one window, no balcony. No one could possibly get in."
—Minosz, Orzhov chief of security
The one thing the Gatewatch didn't expect to find on a plane ruled by Nicol Bolas was perfection.
Some naga initiates move as silently as the suns' reflections on the water.
"Who will miss you, drywalker? A wife? A child? Perhaps they will blame the sea for your fate, and teach future generations to stay far away from it."
A mercurial face sows distrust. Distrust reaps a lonely life.
The Frogtossers thread feathers, bones, and trophies from past raids into their standards, believing they fuel the warren with the anger of its victims.
Beyond pain, beyond obsession and wild despair, there lies a place of twisted power only the most tormented souls can reach.

"By fate or by will, every reign must come to an end."
—Kethis, the Hidden Hand
It shambled from the cloud of ash and bone dust, undeterred by its own extinction.

"His tenement is filled with the most vile, disgusting vermin. It's infested with rats, too."
—Branko One-Ear

"Death is no excuse for disobedience."
—Liliana Vess
"Eldrazi? Ha! Try walking through Zulaport at night with your pockets full. Now *that's* dangerous."
It fears no sword and leaves no bones behind.
Were she not a judge, she'd win the division herself.

"The shortest path between two points is not always the safest."
—Tamina, district guide
"To care for yourself, cultivate the world. To care for the world, cultivate yourself."

"Animals commune with their environment without the need for language. Theirs is a fundamental connection that surpasses flimsy words."
—Vivien Reid
The Roil redraws the world as it passes, leaving only the hedrons unchanged.
"Now is the hour. Ours is the duty. For victory and family—charge!"

"Only the lion knows more stories than I do."
—Chulane, Teller of Tales

"The land grows only where the kami will it."
—Dosan the Falling Leaf

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I, II — Mill two cards, then you may return a creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
III — Return all land cards from your graveyard to the battlefield, then shuffle your graveyard into your library.

faces.f: Her connection to the plane restored, Nissa felt the power of Zendikar surge through her.

"When the land is angry, so are they."
—Nissa Revane
"The curse is broken."
"Dance, and bring forth the coil! It is an umbilical to Gaea herself, fattening us with the earth's rich bounty."
The first satyr to wake after a revel must search for the site of the next one.

"If you threaten its territory, it produces spores. Actually, no matter what you do, it produces spores."
—Hadi Kasten, Calla Dale naturalist
"New growth applies a healing poultice to wounds long scabbed over."
"The land gives of itself. Its abundance provides, even in times of chaos."
One quiet word sets off the stampede.
"Our foes are many and mighty, but not as many as the trees or as mighty as the sea."

"I was wrong. Zendikar isn't after me. It isn't after any of us. It's not evil or vengeful. It's magnificent . . . but it's in pain."
—Nissa Revane
If you want to wreak havoc above, sometimes it's best to look below.

"Taking down a dragon is easy. All you need is enough space to get in a good swing."
—Narbulg Nine Fingers

"The ancient places of Ravnica awaken, stirred by the hoofbeats of Ilharg!"
—Nikya of the Old Ways
Greenweaver Mina and her twin brother Denn lead the last of the Mul Daya into an uncertain future.

"Birth and death are both reversible."
—Nicol Bolas
"It's not a matter of deserving. It's a matter of strength. The power to hold versus the power to take."
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
It spilled the blood of one elder dragon. In Gideon's hands, it may yet taste another's.
It harmonizes with the essence of its master.
A key that slips through every lock.

"Wear this, and take your place among the shadows—wise, lethal, and unseen."
—Ivrelya, Dimir spymaster
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.

"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?"
—Jhoira, master artificer
Fields of battle turn to fields of grain.
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
Enter with merciful hearts. Exit with battle cries.
When defeat is near and guidance is scarce, all eyes look in one direction.
Only when you've given up the search will the caves yield their secrets.
In the cold corridors of the undercity, misinformation unfurls from Duskmantle like a spreading stain.
Every world is an organism, able to grow new lands. Some just do it faster than others.
Enter and leave the shackles of society behind.
On Naya, ambition and treachery are scarce, hunted nearly to extinction by the awe owed to terrestrial gods.
Between the thunderous footfalls of Naya's behemoths lie moments of perfect quiet.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
Enter and rejoice! The Conclave stands united, open to one and all.

"Long after the land has given up the last of its secrets, there will still be mysteries in the depths of the sea."
—Kiora
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
A common foe is the death of old hatreds.
"We shall persevere."

"Archons dispense justice according to an ancient, and flawed, premise."
—Nissa Revane
"My cats have taught me more about the sacred than anything in some old ruin."

"Move, you wretched thing! You're scaring the hurdas!"
—Bruse Tarl, Goma Fada nomad
"I swing a sword. It's a simple life. A lot of adventurers just see me as some cheap muscle, but if my steel lets them return home with their lives and limbs intact, then I've done my job."
"From legend it was forged, and to legend it returns."
"The gifts of the past must find their way into deserving hands."

"Iona no longer guards this place. We do."
—Kasla, Emeria shepherd

"You called it the castle of a god. It is less than that, and so much more."
—Kasla, Emeria shepherd
In any adventuring party, the cleric is the heart: healing wounds, inspiring courage, and raising morale.
"I've walked every one of the Teetering Peaks and never set a foot wrong. I can get you to safety."
Griffins nest in precarious places, so fledglings often find themselves taking their first flights at surprising moments.
Ondu moas make wildly uncomfortable mounts, but for determined warriors, their speed is enough to make up for it.

"Down below's where things go to die."
—Kreq of Sunder Bay

"Wise adventurers—and clever beasties—stick to the higher ground."
—Kreq of Sunder Bay
Too flashy to ignore. Too fast to catch.
Every kor blade is imbued with the skill of a thousand generations.
"The landbind ritual connects us to our sacred sites. More importantly, it binds us with every other kor who has visited here, through countless generations."
"We are many, and righteous."
"Rally to my light, and together we will drive out this darkness!"

"May bloodflies empty your veins and turn you into a dried leather sack, cow!"
—Bruse Tarl, Goma Fada nomad

"They say the wind carved out these canyon walls. But the floor was hammered flat by hooves."
—Kreq of Sunder Bay

"The ground is rumbling. Better hope it's just the Roil!"
—Kreq of Sunder Bay
Its ferocity is tempered by patience, knowing it must wait for just the right moment to strike a killing blow.
"This is my world, Jace, down to its very bones."

"At first rumble you'd best hold on tight and pray to any gods you still hold dear."
—Nys Dal, Sea Gate trapfinder

"It always seems so quiet in the aftermath of wrenching violence."
—Nys Dal, Sea Gate trapfinder
"If we fight as one, nothing can stand in our way!"
Each individual has their own crucial role to play.
Poke a drake in the right place and it becomes as docile as a pet. Poke it in the wrong place and goodbye, hand.
On occasion, felidars leave meaty "gifts" outside the tents of explorers they consider worthy.

"If you practice something often enough, it becomes part of you. That's why we train, and that's why we survive."
—Tasha, Graypelt veteran
The Sea Gate Expeditionary House was founded after the discovery of the Skyclave over Tazeem. Now its banners fly over every corner of Zendikar.

"It blocks the windswept salt and frigid air, but the loneliness of Sejiri remains."
—Enwor, Sea Gate Expeditionary House

"This place offers nothing and takes everything."
—Enwor, Sea Gate Expeditionary House
"Rest, friends. I will protect you."

"Well, she can jump farther than I can."
—Aelah, expedition cleric

"As points of no return go, it is quite epic."
—Aelah, expedition cleric

"Darkness always flees from the light, and I am the breaking dawn."
—Kordain, luminarch of Kabira

"It's good to see the eagles circling the Lighthouse once again."
—Tazri

"I think not."
—Flekon the Mindcensor

"All you minnows in the murk, come to my light."
—Jejenar, Silundi lullmage

"Stay close to my light. You don't want to get lost on the rocks."
—Jejenar, Silundi lullmage
"Perhaps you can't see the path, but that doesn't mean it isn't there."
Zendikar's seas are deeper than anyone can fathom.

"Serves you right for rushing ahead."
—Kaliea, Sea Gate trapfinder
"Before my people turned to false gods, we built a glittering city beneath the northern sea ice. The magic of ancient Benthidrix lives in me!"
"You mess with one of us, you mess with all of us!"
"Come on, Skitch, we'll lose them in the geyserfield."
"I can't see all that the future holds, but I can keep us one step ahead of death."
Wizards' spells twist the fabric of reality to channel elemental energies, peer into the future, and even calm the Roil.
"In the field, speed-reading is a survival skill."

"When I touched the Glasspool, I tasted infinite possibility."
—Ashen Wal, Akoum Expeditionary House

"Past and possibility come together in the vastness of infinite reflection."
—Ashen Wal, Akoum Expeditionary House
In theory, the death of the Eldrazi should have stilled the Roil. It did not.

"You worry too much."
—Nys Dal, Sea Gate trapfinder

"The Ondu Skyclave was a center for rebellion against the capital in Makindi. Of course they built in deadly traps."
—Nys Dal, Sea Gate trapfinder

"If you don't like the weather, just wait a few minutes and it'll change ... probably for the worse."
—Amandi, kitesail expert
"One spell to quiet the Roil, one to quash the will. The principle is the same."
Jace traced Nahiri to the Singing City, but the magic of the ancient ruins threatened to overwhelm his mind.
"For generations, we have bred and trained falcons for expeditions into Emeria. Now more sky ruins open themselves to those with the means to reach the heights!"

"The ancient kor were a clever bunch with a taste for nasty traps. Spikes, poison, fire pouring forth with no warning . . . I've seen and disabled them all. If you intend to raid a Skyclave, you'd be wise to hire me on."

"Most days the sea is my friend. But only most days."
—Jori En, expedition leader
To an explorer, a priceless treasure. To the crab, a rock to call home.

n: Sea Gate Restoration // Sea Gate, Reborn

faces.f:
"We have much to remember ... and much we can never forget."
—Tazri

"We carry on the legacy of those who defended our world by continuing to unearth its secrets."
—Tazri
"Sunken ruins? My specialty."

"Feel the current? Rough waters lie ahead."
—Jori En, expedition leader

"From the hedron fields of Agadeem to the Faduun of Jwar Isle, the islands of the Silundi Sea offer one mystery after another."
—Jori En, expedition leader
An ancient sea monster dragged the Murasa Skyclave under the waves, then smaller sea monsters moved in.
"I've yet to discover the ruin that can keep me out."
"The Roil can be directed. Observe."

"You see a waterfall. I see a way up."
—Ko Dari, expedition wizard

"The source of the Umara River sits high above Oran-Rief, ever weeping on the jungle below."
—Ko Dari, expedition wizard
"It's an ideal method for exploring sky ruins. The drakes sniff me briefly but then lose interest."

"Now is the death-hour, just before dawn. Wake, sleepers, and haunt the living!"
—Vivias, Witch Vessel

"Here below the hedron fields, souls and secrets lie entombed."
—Vivias, Witch Vessel

"If you ever want to get back up, do what I say."
—Exena, expedition rogue

"The Raimunza River flows along the branches of jaddi trees for miles before plunging down to feed Blackbloom Lake."
—Exena, expedition rogue
Blood is the oldest currency.
"We are free. It is our duty to live well."
"He could handle any one of us, but he's no match for all of us!"
Taborax's cultists are the latest in a long history of beings who have desired to see Zendikar torn to pieces.
"Hush."
Its silent slithering belies its bulk.
Rogues bring an array of useful skills to the work of an adventuring party: stealth, agility, the ability to locate and disarm traps, and a subtle, deadly fighting style.

"On vile wings and bloody wind, the swarm will rise."
—Skyclave inscription
Stinking, silent death.
Death comes in many forms on Guul Draz, most of them slow, subtle, and agonizing. At least a monstrous crocodile offers a swift death.

"Din, turn around! Now!"
—Doros, expedition guide

"I think we somehow got turned around."
—Doros, expedition guide
With the bloodchiefs annihilated in the fight between the free and enthralled, the swamps around Malakir are full of dangerous, young vampires eager to make their marks.
Heedless of Nissa's warnings, Nahiri repeated history.
"From your veins to mine."

"Those who fail to escape Malakir become part of the city's defense."
—Doros, expedition guide

"Getting into Malakir isn't difficult. It's getting out that's the hard part."
—Doros, expedition guide
"The vampires never had gods. We followed our bloodchiefs. Now they are gone. What is left? Destruction and death, my friends. That is enough."
"The meal was exquisite. The conversation, less so."
Under Drana's leadership, vampires are finding new strength in unity.
"When navigating dangerous terrain, one hundred legs are better than two."
The Free City of Nimana is a great place to recruit adventurers with shady skill sets.

"Indulge the void. Become the void. Consume all you touch."
—Drana, the last bloodchief

"I knew we shouldn't have come this way."
—Sneeflebrix, expedition rogue

"As a child, I was afraid of the dark. Now, I'm afraid of the things I know are lurking in the dark, waiting to bite my head off."
—Sneeflebrix, expedition rogue
Vampires are now masters of their own fates, commanders of their own legions.
The shadows of death fall over everyone in the end.

—Akiri, kor line-slinger
The Kargan tribes share legends of the victory their ancestors won over the Akoum Skyclave, and its horrendous cost.
Silence is an underrated hunting strategy.

"Look at this place. What more evidence do you require that existence is bleak and meaningless?"
—Voshk, oblivion priest

"I'm not cruel, but I have no patience for your mistakes."
—Tyrux, expedition warrior

—Tyrux, expedition warrior

Every rebirth looks like a death.
Warriors are combat specialists who bring their deadly skills to bear against the many foes that adventurers face in the course of their journeys.
"Down in flames" isn't a destination, but a journey.
He might call up a burst of lava or a raging hellion from Akoum's volcanic depths. Or he might just fall in.

"Her weapon's impressive, sure. But you should see her wield it."
—Gred, expedition warrior
"Everybody grab a leg!"
Naturally inquisitive and adaptable, goblins can turn their small stature to their advantage as rogues.

"The toll is steep, but the cliffs are steeper."
—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House

—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House

"Zendikar has suffered enough. It is time, at last, for my home to know peace."

—Sachir, Akoum Expeditionary House
"Here, you take it!"
"You can cower from the crushing shards or embrace the danger of Akoum. I've made my choice."

"Our feeble villages and tiny encampments stand only at the whim of the Roil."
—*The Invokers' Tales*
"Lava flows where it pleases. I'm just happy to be along for the ride!"

"We just pay him and point him at problems."
—Aro, Sea Gate adventurer

—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House

"A thousand sparks can burn through your defenses just as quickly as one massive blaze."
—Attikar, Akoum elementalist
Wrenched from the ground like a dirt-caked rock, the ancient Skyclave wriggled with life.
"I swear, it's a shortcut."

"I'm not proud of the things I did. But all I could think about at the time was how to make the noise stop."
—Yavotz, Sea Gate Expeditionary House

"They call it the Singing City, but those eerie sounds aren't music. They worm their way into your brain until rational thought is impossible."
—Yavotz, Sea Gate Expeditionary House

"Stop screaming! You'll only bring down more spikes."
—Raff Slugeater, goblin shortcutter

"Silence until we're through. Even a whisper's echo can dislodge death from above."

—Raff Slugeater, goblin shortcutter
"Ready? One... two..."

"Stay away from my friends!"
Kargan tribal lands rarely have issues with goblin raids. Coincidentally, they also rarely have issues keeping their dragons fed.
As with everything else, goblins believe fortifications benefit from as many spiky bits as possible.

—Tars Olan, stoneforge mystic

"I can hear the echo of their hammers, long stilled."
—Tars Olan, stoneforge mystic
Goblin cavalry tactics consist of pointing a beast in a direction and hanging on for as long as possible.
"Good, we're all here. Let's get started!"
When the ruins awakened, so did their defenses.

"Always have a backup plan."
—Doral, Bala Ged guide

"I know it's around here somewhere."
—Doral, Bala Ged guide
Getting airborne with a kitesail is easy. It's everything afterward that takes focus, skill, and luck.

"You can almost see it calculating—are we a tasty enough treat to risk the jump?"
—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House
"I've got a little surprise for you, beasties! Come and get it!"
Where mana flows, the gnarlids follow.
The hatchlings will fill the jungles of Murasa in a glittering tide.
"If you only follow where the paths lead, you merely go where others have gone before you."

—Triel, Kazandu tuskcaller

"The elves stick to the trees. Here, where the trees welcome the sky and leave room for grazing herds—this is our land."

Its hood blossoms as a warning: receive your gift, but stray no closer.

The seeds of memory grow eternal.

—Nissa Revane

"Survival rule 782: There are *always* more scute bugs."
—Zurdi, goblin shortcutter
For use on cliffs and other faces.
Hope and courage bloom in her wake.

—Doral, Bala Ged guide

—Doral, Bala Ged guide

Standing between a scythecat and its prey makes you the appetizer.

"The trees here twist around spikes of mana, feeding off the flowing power."

Made from canvas, wood, and hope.

—Ayli, high priest of the Eternal Pilgrims
